mods.name: MMD OreSpawn
mods.description: A configurable, provider-driven engine for terrain, ores, and underground deposits.

releases.notes:
Version 4.1.1.2602001 (local candidate)

* Keep saved ore settings when a provider renames a recognised rule. Add the
  matching modern rule as a disabled alternative rather than another ore pass.

Version 4.1.0.2602001

* Leave imported vanilla ores inactive while Manage Vanilla Ores is off.
* Use active imported settings instead of adding a second default placement pass when it is on.
* Keep biome and ore-list text visible with Minecraft's ARGB renderer.
* Move Help & Guide beside Recommended Defaults and fit both main menus above the footer.
* Reject invalid geome IDs without changing their spelling.
* Recognise inline vanilla ore features without changing mixed or unknown outputs.
* Release ore wrappers when a server stops and keep their shared biome ordering.
* Add shared-ore Eclipse profiles and real Nether fresh/reload checks.
* Use Minecraft Mod Development as the jar vendor and replay cold builds offline.
* Add the mod directory, material-group ore controls, and built-in MMD conflict defaults.
* Add exact new-terrain biome replacement and dimension-wide material controls.
* Preserve old profiles and missing-mod settings when upgrading schemas to 5, 8, and 7.
* Split the build into smaller commented scripts and normalize tracked text to LF.

Version 4.0.16.2602001

* Leave benchmark shutdown to the GameTest harness when a benchmark is run
  through Forge's GameTest server, preventing a null test-tracker crash and
  allowing the harness to report its real test result.
* Ordinary dedicated benchmark servers still stop automatically when requested.

Version 4.0.15.2602001

* Classify generated geology and public geology samples through the same
  stable quart-biome cell at three-dimensional biome boundaries.
* Keep ore family-host filters and sampler predictions consistent when later
  surface features alter the final heightmap by a small amount.
* Existing chunks, profiles, API signatures, and schemas are unchanged.

Version 4.0.14.2602001

* Convert naturally exposed one-layer Snow at the first free block above the
  motion-blocking surface while retaining the existing Snow and Ice scan.
* Preserve buried or authored Snow and Ice, unconfigured dimensions, fluids,
  bedrock, block entities, profiles, schemas, and existing chunks.

Version 4.0.13.2602001

* Give the public ore-dimension builder the exact biome include/exclude and
  biome-dictionary filter support already available in provider JSON.
* Accept valid namespaced geome IDs in both creation-editor validation paths
  while preserving legacy unnamespaced geome keys.
* API major 1, schemas, existing profiles, generated chunks, and worldgen
  behaviour are unchanged.

Version 4.0.12.2602001

* Classify public geology samples at the same highest occupied block used by
  chunk geology generation, rather than the first free block above it.
* Keep public sampler predictions consistent with generated rock at vertical
  biome seams without changing existing chunks, profiles, or generation.

Version 4.0.11.2602001

* Preserve biome-dictionary geome weights when a data-driven biome is reached
  through its stable registry key rather than the object baked at startup.
* Apply ore biome include and exclude filters by stable registry key so
  dynamic-registry biome instances with the same ID are treated consistently.
* Existing chunks and profile formats are unchanged; the corrections apply to
  generation in affected provider biomes.

Version 4.0.10.2602001

* Evaluate Stable Layers rock min_y and max_y bounds against actual world Y
  instead of the vertically shifted formation coordinate.
* Preserve the shifted formation identity for layer, family, and rock choice
  while preventing vanilla Stone fallback near dimension floors and ceilings.
* Apply the correction only while generating new chunks; existing chunks and
  saved profiles remain unchanged.

mods.name: MMD OreSpawn
mods.description: A configurable, provider-driven engine for terrain, ores, and underground deposits.

releases.notes:
Version 4.1.6.113021

* Leave vanilla ores to Minecraft when Manage Vanilla Ores is off. When
  it is on, an imported rule takes over without an extra copy of the ore.
* Keep saved Ore Sources choices for imported patterns. Built-in patterns
  share the standard channel for new choices; custom channels stay separate.
* Show vanilla ores in Ore Sources before creating a world, even when Manage
  Vanilla Ores is off.
* Keep imported provider rules when opening a saved world. Back up the
  profile before removing an untouched duplicate; keep edited rules for review.
* Choose sulfur and lithium defaults after mods have loaded, including Base
  Electric. Existing worlds keep their choices.
* Fix the Austrian German language ID and add Pirate Speak menu and guide text.

Version 4.1.0.113021

* Fix managed Nether quartz hosts on Forge 1.13.2, including saved profiles
  that refer to the absent forge:netherrack tag. Existing chunks stay untouched.
  New Nether ore and fluid-deposit rules also use the installed netherrack block.
* Add a directory for loaded provider mods and optional add-on settings screens.
* Group OreSpawn-managed ores by exact block tags. Balanced, Single, Custom,
  and Keep Original policies keep one placement budget per channel without
  changing existing worlds' saved behaviour.
* Add a biome directory with exact new-terrain replacement, palette settings,
  and dimension-wide materials controls. Existing chunks are never rewritten.
* Preserve missing-mod settings and dormant imported Ore Dictionary aliases.
  Provider, global, and world schemas are now 5, 8, and 7; API major remains 1.
* Keep the 4.0.16 Forge 1.13-specific behaviour: this target has neither
  three-dimensional biome-cell attribution nor a server-side GameTest harness.

Version 4.0.14.113021

* Convert exposed one-layer vanilla Snow from the first free cell immediately
  above Minecraft's motion-blocking surface when a dimension supplies a custom
  snow material.
* Retain the existing surface Ice conversion and leave buried or authored Snow
  and Ice unchanged.

Version 4.0.13.113021

* Give the public ore-dimension builder the exact biome include/exclude and
  biome-dictionary filter support already available in provider JSON.
* Accept valid namespaced geome IDs in both creation-editor validation paths
  while preserving legacy unnamespaced geome keys.
* API major 1, schemas, existing profiles, generated chunks, and worldgen
  behaviour are unchanged.

Version 4.0.10.113021

* Evaluate Stable Layers rock min_y and max_y bounds against actual world Y
  instead of the vertically shifted formation coordinate.
* Preserve the shifted formation identity for layer, family, and rock choice
  while preventing vanilla Stone fallback near dimension floors and ceilings.
* Apply the correction only while generating new chunks; existing chunks and
  saved profiles remain unchanged.

Version 4.0.9.113021

* Replace provider-declared natural terrain hosts during the existing geology
  scan before structure and vegetation features can author matching blocks.
* Keep air, fluids, bedrock, and block entities protected even when their block
  IDs are mistakenly declared as terrain hosts.
* Apply the correction only while generating new chunks; existing chunks and
  saved profiles remain unchanged.

Version 4.0.8.113021

* Preserve long host, tag, and biome-list values when OreSpawn editors load
  and save an existing profile without user changes.
* Add reproducible ForgeGradle 7 builds, audited release artifacts, SHA-256
  checksums, Buildship launches, and guarded release automation.
* Export the complete bundled guide, including the shared version policy, to
  the player-facing configuration folder.
* Forge 1.12.2's 4.0.7 packaged access-transformer repair is target-specific
  and is not applicable to Forge 1.13.2.

Version 4.0.6.113021

* Adopt target-qualified four-component versions so Minecraft and loader compatibility can be identified from the mod version.


...

Version 4.1.6.112021

* Let Java providers select an exact ore host, such as plain stone without
  granite. Whole-block selectors still work as before.
* Keep imported ore rules and saved choices when moving a world from 1.10.2
  or 1.11.2. Back up the profile before removing an untouched duplicate and
  leave edited rules for review.
* Choose sulfur and lithium defaults after all mods have loaded so Base
  Electric can share the same veins. Existing worlds keep their choices.
* Use the correct Austrian German locale and give Pirate Speak its own menu
  and guide text.

Version 4.1.3.112021

* Apply hybrid and replacement background limits to imported built-in ore
  patterns, just as for ordinary native rules. Keep explicit channels and
  third-party deposit patterns independent.
* Retain older Ore Sources selections under their saved pattern names without
  rewriting imported settings or regenerating existing chunks.
* Show imported placement choices in the editor without duplicate old-channel
  rows. Distinguish an inactive source from a missing mod, and keep custom
  channels and saved choices intact.
* Keep the empty Ore Sources message inside its pane in smaller windows.
* Remove old 1.10-only ABI test tasks that could start an empty server on 1.12.

Version 4.1.2.112021

* Respect Manage Vanilla Ores for imported OS1/OS3 rules. With it off, leave
  vanilla ore generation alone and keep those rules saved but inactive.
* With vanilla management on, use the imported placement settings without
  adding a second Minecraft or OreSpawn default pass. Keep saved settings,
  dimension limits and existing chunks unchanged.

Version 4.1.1.112021

* Keep existing provider settings when importing older ore files for the first
  time, instead of replacing them with the older settings.
* Describe preserved settings as retained rather than verified in the upgrade
  report. Invalid files are still checked by the normal provider loader.

Version 4.1.0.112021

* Clarify dimension-wide material controls and replace light-equivalent custom
  aquifer-fluid injection with an exact one-shot generation mask, preserving
  surfaces, caves and later decorator fluids while keeping generation near the
  native path. Differently lit fluids retain the compatible generator path.
* Replace the first-palette-only biome editor with a responsive biome directory
  that reports every loaded, referenced and missing biome once, together with
  palette ownership, effective order, placement count and surface conflicts.
  Its dimension selector filters routine entries through Forge biome domains
  while retaining explicit placement, replacement and missing-provider rules.
* Add exact one-to-one biome replacements for newly generated terrain through a
  reserved terminal palette which always runs after ordinary provider/profile
  palettes. Replacement chains flatten, cycles are rejected and missing targets
  remain dormant until their owning mod returns. Valid unmanaged targets no
  longer produce a misleading warning or duplicate new-terrain notice.
* Expose palette enablement, placement weights, climate and dependency limits,
  surfaces, namespace scope, region size, coverage, fallback weight, dimension
  materials and geome influences without adding arbitrary weighted biome output.
* Add confirmed biome, palette, dimension and all-biome resets. Active providers
  return to their shipped defaults, user-only palettes are removed and entries
  owned by missing providers are preserved; all changes retain Done/Cancel
  editor-session semantics and never rewrite existing chunks.
* Add Ore Sources policies that group equivalent configured outputs by material
  and dimension while keeping ordinary and custom placement channels independent.
* Consolidate only reviewed high-confidence MMD conflicts for new worlds;
  upgraded worlds retain their previous separate placement and output behaviour.
* Select one weighted output for an entire ordinary vein or custom deposit body
